source.title: Accordion: Adaptive Gradient Communication via Critical Learning Regime Identification
source.authors: Saurabh Agarwal; Hongyi Wang; Kangwook Lee; S. Venkataraman; Dimitris Papailiopoulos

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some table layouts are flattened, so table values that cannot be assigned confidently are not reconstructed.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether larger batches affect held-out accuracy under fixed epoch budgets and whether an adaptive schedule can mitigate the effect; its batch-size intervention is a conceptual test of V5.
record.gate_note: The paper also discusses critical learning regimes and reports results for gradient compression, but those results do not test the listed versions about random-label memorization, network width, convolutional bias, optimizer choice, dropout, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares batch sizes using held-out accuracy under the same 300-epoch budget, and tests whether batch-size scheduling with learning-rate scaling mitigates the penalty. These are the intervention and measure named in V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the batch-size findings but omits the paper's main conclusion about adaptive gradient compression. The authors conclude that detecting critical regimes enables adaptive compression to preserve held-out performance while reducing communication. Extending the approach to batch-size scheduling matches small-batch accuracy in the reported 512/4096 experiments without additional tuning beyond the stated recipe, but leaves approximately 1.6% accuracy loss when scaling CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 to batch 16,384.
record.recipe_differences: Uses adaptive batch-size scheduling with learning-rate scaling and warmup; evaluates distributed training on CIFAR datasets under a fixed epoch budget.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported accuracy loss appears at batch size 16,384; the batch-size 512/4096 comparison uses learning-rate scaling when switching and five epochs of warmup.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradient-compression schedules affect accuracy and communication on image classifiers and a WikiText-2 LSTM; gradient-norm changes also identify proposed critical regimes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The timing and strength of gradient compression affect final held-out performance, and adaptive compression can mitigate its accuracy cost.

record.problems: Only three independent trials are reported. Specific confidence intervals for the table values are not stated in the supplied text. Some table formatting is flattened.
record.rows_left_out: Other architecture and dataset entries appear in Tables 5 and 6, but the supplied flattened table layout does not permit confident assignment of all displayed numbers to model, dataset, and condition; they are omitted rather than reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.
Language-model batch-size effects, longer-training remedies, normalization or regularization remedies, and systematic identification of workload-dependent critical batch sizes.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on data size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Training-phase batch-size controls comparing small batches in critical regimes with large batches in critical regimes, alongside constant-batch controls. These distinguish schedule timing from simply using a larger batch.
The Smith et al. batch-size schedule comparison: the authors explicitly report that it fails to match small-batch accuracy on CIFAR-100, whereas Accordion matches it under the same epoch budget.

record.verdict_notes: The flattened tables interleave CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 entries; Figures 16 and 17 corroborate the dataset correction for R1–R3. Other architecture/dataset table entries are already declared in rows_left_out and are therefore not repeated as missing. Results average three independent trials; numerical confidence intervals are unavailable in the supplied text. The study is not an original source for V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Language-model batch-size comparisons and comparisons across workload-dependent critical batch sizes.
Dropout effects and interaction with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and comparing with random removals.
